feed.title: Singletrack Sessions

bullets: Enduro racing is about risk management rather than nerve; a clear framing of risk matters more than bravado on the trail.
Season-ending crashes are almost never the scary-looking ones; they come from the boring risk you didn't name, which is why overlooked hazards deserve the most attention.
Naming the risk before it names you removes half the danger, because a risk you can describe is one you can design around.
A race run should be ridden as a whole system rather than a list of corners, since mistakes come from how one section sets up the next.
A full season of self-logged crashes showed the causes were always two turns upstream, meaning the root error happens well before the point of failure.
A race line and a portfolio share the same discipline; both are systems of correlated bets where the real work is managing the interactions rather than individual choices.
